stemMd: A cyclist travels 120 m east and then 50 m west in 20 s. What is the magnitude of average velocity?
explanationMd: Average velocity uses displacement, not total path length. Net displacement is 120 − 50 = 70 m east, so its magnitude divided by 20 s is 3.5 m s⁻¹. Average speed would instead use 170 m and is larger.

distractorRationale.a: This is total distance divided by time, the average speed.
distractorRationale.d: This ignores the westward part of the journey.
distractorRationale.e: This uses only the westward distance.
distractorRationale.b: The cyclist does not return to the starting point.
